# imgt

> A small, self-hosted image optimizer on Cloudflare. Sharp resizes public images to WebP; Workers Cache and a private R2 bucket cache derivatives. Original images are never stored.

`GET /image?url=<encoded-HTTPS-source>&w=<width>&q=<quality>` returns WebP.
Use `URLSearchParams` to encode the source. Width is required; quality defaults
to 77. Default widths: 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384, 640, 750, 828, 1080,
1200, 1920, 2048, 3840. Default qualities: 60, 75, 77, 85.

`ALLOWED_HOSTS` is a Worker environment variable containing original image
hostnames. Set it as Text in Cloudflare's Worker Settings → Variables and Secrets,
then select Deploy. The starter uses `keep_vars: true` and leaves this variable
out of `wrangler.jsonc` so dashboard values survive code deployments. An explicit
`vars.ALLOWED_HOSTS` would override the dashboard value even with `keep_vars`.
The frontend belongs here only if it serves originals. Exact entries allow
only that host; `*.example.com` allows subdomains but excludes `example.com`.
An empty list denies all sources; every redirect is checked against the list.
Sources must be public HTTPS URLs. Inputs: JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF, up to
25 MiB and 50 megapixels. Small images are not enlarged.

For Next.js, use the TypeScript custom loader in the guide below. Keep widths
and qualities aligned with `imgt.config.ts`. Relative local assets need a
public HTTPS origin. `GET /health` checks Worker configuration; use the smoke
command in the deployment guide to verify the image pipeline.

These Markdown resources are served from this deployment without GitHub access.
For local development, copy `.dev.vars.example` to `.dev.vars`.
